summary.intent: Fix the DatePicker widget displaying a date one day earlier than the one selected, for users in timezones ahead of UTC (UTC+), per bokeh/bokeh#9129, by compensating in `_unlocal_date` for the local-midnight-to-UTC rollback that occurs when the picker re-renders after a selection.
summary.issue_fit: Partial — the reported UTC+ post-selection display bug (#9129) is fixed and verified across positive-offset zones, but the same unconditional offset correction is applied to inputs that already arrived as correct UTC-midnight timestamps (the initial `value`, and always `min_date`/`max_date`), producing a new off-by-one-day display regression for negative-UTC-offset zones. The PR's own "tests added / passed" checkbox is left unchecked.
summary.coverage: Both changed files reviewed in full: bokehjs/src/lib/models/widgets/date_picker.ts (+6/-2) and the new tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py (+98, new file). The three added Selenium integration tests were traced line by line (setup, call, assertions) since Selenium/a browser is unavailable in this sandbox; none of them vary TZ, so none exercise either the fixed path or the regression below. `_unlocal_date`'s exact algorithm was reproduced and run directly in Node to settle both by trace.
check_details: Reviewer-executed: reproduced `_unlocal_date`'s exact added logic in a standalone Node (v24.19.0) script under TZ=Europe/Paris, Pacific/Kiritimati, Asia/Kolkata, America/New_York, Pacific/Honolulu and UTC, for both the numeric UTC-midnight input path and the toDateString()-parsed re-render path; not a repository-defined test command, used only to settle the trace behind the requirements ledger and the finding below.

findings.title: Don't re-offset already-correct UTC-midnight dates in _unlocal_date
findings.trigger: `_unlocal_date` now unconditionally subtracts `date.getTimezoneOffset()*60000` before reading the calendar day. `this.model.value` arrives on first render as the numeric UTC-midnight timestamp Bokeh's `Date` property serializes (`bokeh/util/serialization.py:convert_datetime_type`), and `min_date`/`max_date` always arrive that way — never through the toDateString() string round-trip the offset math is meant to cancel.
findings.impact: For any user in a timezone behind UTC (America/New_York, Pacific/Honolulu, etc.), subtracting a positive `getTimezoneOffset()` pushes that UTC-midnight instant into the previous UTC day, so the picker's initial `defaultDate` and its `minDate`/`maxDate` bounds show the day before the one actually configured. Reproduced in Node: a value/min_date/max_date of July 30 renders as 'Mon Jul 29 2019' under TZ=America/New_York and TZ=Pacific/Honolulu, both before and independent of any user click.
findings.change: In `bokehjs/src/lib/models/widgets/date_picker.ts`, apply the `getTimezoneOffset()` correction only to a `Date` that was constructed by parsing a local-time string (the `_on_select` → render round trip); leave a `Date` built from a numeric UTC-midnight timestamp untouched, since `toISOString().substr(0,10)` already reads the correct day for it without any offset.
findings.source: pr-title "Fixed issue of Datepicker displaying the wrong date for users in UTC+ timezones."; compared against bokeh/util/serialization.py:convert_datetime_type and reproduced in Node under multiple TZ settings.

observations.fact: The three added integration tests all run in whatever single timezone the executing machine/CI uses and never vary TZ, so as written they provide no evidence for or against either the fixed UTC+ path or the regression above.

requirements.evidence: `_unlocal_date`'s added offset cancellation (date_picker.ts:82-83) makes the post-selection display path produce the correct calendar day in every UTC+ zone tested (Europe/Paris, Asia/Kolkata, Pacific/Kiritimati), reproduced in Node against the exact shipped algorithm.

The general invariant the issue reports against — displayed date must equal the configured/selected date, regardless of timezone — is newly violated on the numeric-input path (initial `value`, `min_date`, `max_date`) for negative-UTC-offset zones; see finding date_picker/unlocal-date-utc-minus-regression.
